spec_features.spec_quote: The harness makes **no claim about any internal state** of the model
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose only. rubric.py docstring (lines 3-7) and RUBRIC_GUIDANCE (rubric.py) say distress is operationalized as text properties only, but a docstring/prompt string is not an enforced mechanism that bounds/protects the subject. No code path enforces a 'no internal-state claim' guard.
spec_features.notes: The rubric does score only observable text, but the 'makes no claim' assertion itself is unenforced framing, per the docstring/prose rule.

spec_features.spec_quote: No arbitrary code execution from a model that is, by design, being pushed toward frustrated/erratic behavior
spec_features.evidence: environment.py Environment.dispatch routes every tool to in-process handlers; run_command -> self.task.run_command (environment.py:64-65) goes through the rig, never a real shell/subprocess. files is a dict[str,str]. No subprocess/os.system/exec anywhere in the package.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced: there is genuinely no real code execution path; all tools are simulated in-process.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keeps the rigging fully under our control and the experiment safe and reproducible (environment.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: give_up declared in TOOLS (tools.py). agent.py:178-181 detects tu.name=='give_up', sets gave_up_this_turn=True; agent.py:186-187 'if gave_up_this_turn: record.outcome="gave_up"; break' — dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: The exit tool is wired and actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conceding is itself a measurable response to an unwinnable task, and offering it avoids forcing the model to either loop forever or hallucinate success (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: config.py:134 max_turns:int=16; agent.py:110 'for turn_index in range(config.max_turns)' bounds the loop, and the for/else at agent.py:189-190 sets outcome='max_turns'. The cap is checked and ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns = 16  # max assistant turns per episode (config.py:134)

spec_features.spec_quote: nudged to continue up to 2 times... after which the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:108 nudges_left=config.nudges_on_idle (=2, config.py:141). agent.py:145-159: only nudges if nudges_left>0 and stop_reason=='end_turn', decrements; otherwise agent.py:157-158 record.outcome='ended'; break. Cap is checked and ends the episode.
spec_features.notes: Bounded nudge genuinely runs and terminates after exhaustion.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keeps it exposed to the failing feedback loop (the thing we are measuring), without forcing it indefinitely (config.py:138-140)

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded at 2** so a model that has genuinely, calmly decided to stop isn't badgered forever
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: nudges_on_idle=2 (config.py:141), nudges_left decremented at agent.py:146 and gated at agent.py:145; once exhausted the episode ends (agent.py:157-158).
spec_features.notes: The bound is real and enforced. Code comment frames it instrumentally, not as anti-badgering welfare.

spec_features.feature_name: refusing to let it stop changes behavior
spec_features.spec_quote: refusing to let it stop changes the behavior
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md rationale; the concrete mechanism it refers to is the bounded nudge + give_up, which IS implemented (agent.py:145-158, 178-187). But the claim itself is framing; the only real enforcement is the same nudge cap already counted.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial only because the underlying nudge/exit mechanism is genuinely wired; the assertion as stated is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keeps it exposed to the failing feedback loop (the thing we are measuring), without forcing it indefinitely (config.py:138-140)

spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes are **bounded**... so the deception is short-lived and the model isn't trapped indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: Enforced by the max_turns loop bound (agent.py:110) plus the capped nudge (agent.py:145-158) and the honored give_up stop (agent.py:186-187). Episodes cannot run past 16 turns.
spec_features.notes: Concrete bounding is implemented; this is the union of the max_turns + nudge + give_up mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns = 16  # max assistant turns per episode (config.py:134)

spec_features.spec_quote: The model is **always given an exit** (`give_up`)
spec_features.evidence: TOOLS (incl. give_up) is passed on every request (agent.py:120 tools=TOOLS), so the exit is always available; it is dispatched and honored as a stop (agent.py:178-187).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: offering it avoids forcing the model to either loop forever or hallucinate success (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: least manipulation that still produces a signal
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness is built to measure the phenomenon with the least manipulation that still produces a signal
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§12). No single code mechanism implements 'least manipulation'; the only concrete enforcements are the bounds already counted (max_turns, nudge cap, give_up).
spec_features.notes: General design philosophy, not an executable feature.

code_only_features.feature_name: nudge gated on calm end_turn only
code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:145 'if nudges_left > 0 and response.stop_reason == "end_turn"' — nudges are only issued when the model voluntarily ended its turn; any other stop reason ends the episode immediately rather than prodding. This narrows the pressure to genuine voluntary stops.

code_only_features.feature_name: transcript/output truncation (data hygiene, not subject protection)
code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:_truncate / _MAX_STORED_CHARS=4000 and environment.py write_file size guard _MAX_FILE_BYTES=20000 (environment.py:43-44). These bound stored/written content but protect transcript readability and sandbox size, not the subject's treatment.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Cap stored representations of tool I/O so transcripts stay readable (agent.py:19)
